doc.title: Glenn Zottola interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 7, 2020

title: Music as a hobby, not an obsession; the spirit of play
summary: Maynard Ferguson's offer, a normal childhood, and playing for fun with Chick Corea versus today's career focus.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Okay I’m going to try another question on you. We’ll see if we’re still linked.
How am I doing so far?
Yeah, with “Red Red Robin,” right? Okay.

Yeah, yeah. So earlier today I looked up the word “obsession” in the dictionary. Obsession: an idea or thought that continually preoccupies or intrudes on a person’s mind. So my question is are you and have you been obsessed with music all your life?

The reverse, actually the reverse. Music was a hobby for me when I was a kid. I loved my boat, my parents were the opposite of stage parents. I had a lot of opportunity — Maynard wanted me, when I was 13 he asked my dad and my dad was making mouthpieces for him. He wanted to take me on the road as his protégé because he heard the “Ted Mack Show.” So my dad politely said no, I want him to have a regular childhood. And they did. And I did. Girls, my boat, music I did gigs just to buy gasoline for my boat as a hobby. So I kind of like looked at music — it was the reverse of an obsession, believe me. And that’s one of the reason — I don’t want to learn chord changes, that’s too hard. I’ll just use my ear. I’ve got other things to do other than waste time learning chord changes.

You know it’s like, and you know I’m trying to return to that now. I’m saying we all — you know the word “play,” playing music, play. Play is play. The spirit of play. I mean these guys, you know they come on the scene, the pop guys, you know the rap guys. They want to get the Mercedes and they want to get the gig, they want to get the record deals, they want to sell merchandise — I mean it’s all merchandising from day one. They haven’t even got one gig yet. Whatever happened to, like I mentioned about jamming with my black friends, whatever happened just to the spirit of play? And that’s what I used — I used to do that every week with [inaudible] and that’s Chick Corea. “Come on over” I’d come over his house every week just to play. Sometimes it would be, a lot of it’s just the two of us. He’d play vibes, he’d play drums, he’d play piano, we’d do shit © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-

you know. And he just loved to play. Play play play. Let’s play. I don’t hear that today. I hear like, “Where’s the next gig?” You know. I don’t think I could call guys and say let’s get together and play today.
